Published online:

Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Warsh delivered hawkish remarks Friday, sharply lifting September rate hike odds from ~35% to 64%. Markets are on edge ahead of the August jobs report (consensus: +55K), with a back-to-back jobs decline seen as the key threshold that could block the Fed from hiking. CPI (Sep 11) and PPI (Sep 10) are the next critical data points before the Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting. The dollar is near two-week highs, the yen slipped past 160 before recovering on Bessent's comments signaling potential BoJ action. Oil is up 2%+ on Gulf tensions.

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 70 — Warsh's remarks are explicitly hawkish and deliberate, Bessent's yen comments add further policy tightening narrative globally, and futures markets have meaningfully repriced toward a September hike. The only dovish counterweight is the downside jobs risk, which is conditional.
